options.name: React 18 with TypeScript and Redux Toolkit

options.tradeoff: Requires managing boilerplate and some complex state patterns
options.concern: Potential overengineering for smaller components and app parts

options.name: Vue 3 with Composition API and Pinia
options.upside: Simpler syntax and faster onboarding for new developers
options.tradeoff: Smaller ecosystem than React, fewer enterprise integrations
options.concern: May require extra effort for complex state management
options.best_for: teams valuing quick development and ease of use

options.name: SvelteKit with TypeScript and built-in stores
options.upside: Highly performant with minimal runtime overhead
options.tradeoff: Smaller community and fewer third-party libraries
options.concern: Less mature tooling and potential risk for long-term support
options.best_for: teams focused on performance and modern architecture

options.name: Angular 14 with RxJS and NgRx state management
options.upside: Comprehensive framework with strong conventions and enterprise features
options.tradeoff: Steep learning curve and more verbose codebase
options.concern: Risk of slower iteration and developer burnout
options.best_for: teams needing robust structure and long-term enterprise support

Today we're deciding: Choose a framework for the front-end rewrite.
For this simulated decision, I’ll treat the following setup as the shared facts.
Options:
A) React 18 with TypeScript and Redux Toolkit — community support: very large; development speed: fast; learning curve: medium (+ Widely adopted with strong ecosystem and type safety; − Requires managing boilerplate and some complex state patterns)
B) Vue 3 with Composition API and Pinia — community support: large; development speed: very fast; learning curve: low (+ Simpler syntax and faster onboarding for new developers; − Smaller ecosystem than React, fewer enterprise integrations)
C) SvelteKit with TypeScript and built-in stores — community support: medium; development speed: medium; learning curve: medium (+ Highly performant with minimal runtime overhead; − Smaller community and fewer third-party libraries)
D) Angular 14 with RxJS and NgRx state management — community support: large; development speed: medium; learning curve: high (+ Comprehensive framework with strong conventions and enterprise features; − Steep learning curve and more verbose codebase)
Context: The team has exactly 6 developers involved in the rewrite; The project deadline is 6 months from now; The budget allows moderate investment in training or new tooling.
What trade-offs between developer productivity, performance, and long-term maintainability matter most for our front-end rewrite?
